previous_disclosures.summary: QCT is a leading developer and supplier of integrated circuits and system software for mobile devices, automotive systems, and IoT. Its technology roadmap results from extensive collaboration with industry partners and research into emerging standards, leveraging foundational mobile technologies to extend into automotive and IoT applications.

The Snapdragon family includes mobile, compute, sound, and automotive platforms comprising application processors, cellular modems, and wireless connectivity capabilities. Key components include Qualcomm Oryon and Kryo CPUs, Hexagon NPUs for AI processing, and Adreno GPUs.

QCT provides wireless connectivity products for Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and location services across mobile devices, automotive, and IoT applications, including standalone Wi-Fi and Bluetooth products. Networking products include Wi-Fi, Ethernet, and PON chips that enable home and business networks.

current_disclosures.summary: QCT develops a technology roadmap for mobile, automotive, and IoT devices through collaboration with industry partners. Its product families include Snapdragon and Dragonwing, which feature application processors (Oryon, Kryo CPUs), Hexagon NPUs, and Adreno GPUs. In addition to core SoCs, QCT supplies supporting components such as RF transceivers, power management ICs, and integrated Snapdragon 5G modem-RF products that use AI. QCT also provides wireless connectivity products for Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and location services, as well as networking products like Wi-Fi and Ethernet chips.

peer_results.rationale: No candidate is sufficiently comparable. AMD's disclosures focus on embedded computing portfolios (CPUs, APUs, FPGAs, Adaptive SoCs) for automotive, industrial, and networking markets, whereas the target QCOM disclosure focuses on integrated Snapdragon platforms for mobile, compute, sound, and automotive sectors with specific emphasis on AI/NPU and modem integration. The product architectures and primary market verticals (embedded/enterprise vs. mobile/consumer SoC) are fundamentally different despite both being semiconductor companies.

comparisons.peer_summary: The company provides Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and GPS/GNSS solutions for mobile devices, including integrated combination chips and location platform services.
comparisons.comparison: Both QCOM and AVGO disclose wireless connectivity capabilities (Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, GPS/GNSS) as integral components of their mobile platform offerings. QCOM describes these as part of the Snapdragon family's application processors and wireless connectivity capabilities, while AVGO provides discrete and integrated Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and GPS/GNSS solutions specifically designed for mobile devices. AVGO further details the use of combination chips for integrated functionality, a strategy similar to QCOM's system-based integrated solutions.

sentences.text: Each platform consists of application processors and wireless connectivity capabilities, including our cellular modem that provides core baseband modem functionality for voice and data communications, non-cellular wireless connectivity (such as Wi-Fi and Bluetooth) and global positioning functions.

• Connectivity Solutions: Our connectivity solutions include discrete and integrated Wi-Fi and Bluetooth solutions, and global positioning system/global navigation satellite system ("GPS/GNSS") receivers, designed for use in mobile devices including smartphones, tablets and wearable products.
These solutions include combination chips that offer integrated Wi-Fi and Bluetooth functionality, which provides significant performance advantages over discrete solutions.
